preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner
Contract must have accumulated token balance from fees (at least _minTokenBalance)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As owner, set _percentageOfLiquidityForMarketing to >100 (e.g., 1000) via setPercentageOfLiquidityForMarketing(). Then trigger swapAndLiquify by having a user transfer tokens (if contract has accumulated fee tokens). This will cause all BNB from token swaps to be sent to marketing/investing wallets instead of adding liquidity, allowing owner to drain contract's BNB balance to controlled addresses.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has owner-only functions that allow the owner to exclude addresses from fees and change fee recipient addresses. By setting the attacker address as the marketing wallet and excluding it from fees, we can receive the majority of BNB collected from token swaps.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the owner to: 1) Exclude attacker from fees, 2) Set attacker as marketing wallet, 3) Trigger swapAndLiquify to collect BNB fees.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get owner address from contract. 2. Start prank as owner. 3. Call setExcludedFromFee(attacker, true). 4. Call setMarketingWallet(attacker). 5. Transfer tokens to contract to build up contract balance. 6. Trigger swapAndLiquify by transferring tokens (which will trigger auto-swap when contract balance > minTokenBalance).
attempts.feedback: EVM Revert: Economic Exploit Failed: No profit: 79228162514264337593543950335 <= 79228162514264337593543950335。请调整参数或调用路径。

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract collects fees on transfers (13% liquidity fee). When swapAndLiquify is triggered, it converts half of contract's token balance to BNB, and 99% of that BNB goes to marketing wallet. As owner, we can set attacker as marketing wallet and trigger the swap.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate owner to set attacker as marketing wallet. 2. Buy tokens to generate fees for contract. 3. Manually trigger swapAndLiquify by calling it directly (if possible) or by making transfers that trigger it.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get owner and impersonate. 2. Set attacker as marketing and investing wallets. 3. Buy tokens to generate contract fee balance. 4. Ensure contract has enough tokens (> _minTokenBalance). 5. Trigger swapAndLiquify.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous exploit didn't actually increase attacker's BNB balance. The oracle checks NATIVE balance increase, but we were only manipulating token balances. We need to make the contract accumulate BNB from trading fees and then trigger swapAndLiquify to send that BNB to us as marketing wallet.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: We successfully exploited the owner privilege to set ourselves as marketing wallet and received BNB from swapAndLiquify. The transaction just needs to complete without revert.
attempts.attack_strategy: Use 99% marketing fee (default) instead of 100% to leave some BNB for liquidity addition. This will allow the transaction to complete while we still get most of the BNB.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Set marketing fee to 99% (default). 2. Trigger swapAndLiquify. 3. Ensure transaction completes successfully.
attempts.failure_reflection: The exploit is actually working - we received 9.918e18 BNB as marketing fee! However, the transaction reverts at the end because with 100% marketing fee, there's no BNB left for liquidity addition. We need to use a percentage that allows the transaction to complete successfully.
